subject: Interop showcase readout + concrete next-tests for migration proof
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kaplan <sara@bluewave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Interop showcase readout + concrete next-tests for migration proof

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Short readout and proposed next-steps so we all have the same view. I recorded the demo and attached the compatibility matrix we walked through.

Recap (5 bullets):
- Current ask: validate that BlueWave can migrate our captioning inference from HyperscalerX to Redwood with minimal prompt/SDK changes and no regression in latency or token-cost.
- Today’s demo: Redwood served your canonical 3-step prompt set (prep -> summarize -> annotate) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints and returned identical schema + role-handling for 96/100 prompts in the suite.
- Mismatches we saw: two edge cases around streaming finalization (partial chunk ordering) and one prompt that relied on a Hyperscaler-specific token-escape behavior.
- Perf summary (live): median 90th-pct latency across the set was ~120ms lower on Redwood for short prompts; for long-sequence prompts our batching heuristics reduced cost by ~18% in the session we ran.
- Risk: SDK client differences (client-side retry/backoff and streaming frame handling) are the most likely friction point during migration, not the model outputs themselves.

Proposed next-tests (concrete, orderable):
1) OpenAI-compat smoke run: run your 5k prompt QA set through Redwood’s compatibility layer (same HTTP surface as OpenAI) and produce a per-prompt diff report (diff types: token-level, JSON-schema, role-mismatch). Outcome: A pass/fail list + 10 flagged prompts to pair-debug. (Owner: Ben)
2) SDK swap smoke: our SDK -> your prod client (1:1 SDK replacement) with a focus on streaming framing and retry semantics. We'll supply a small shim you can run in CI. (Owner: Vanessa)
3) Latency/cost comparison: run a matched load (50 qps sustained) against HyperscalerX and Redwood for 24h using identical prompts and tokenization settings. Produce per-route cost delta. (Owner: Jordan)
4) Root-cause session for streaming reordering: capture a failing prompt end-to-end, attach KV cache state, and reproduce locally. (Owner: Redwood engineering l2)

Attachments: interop-demo-recording.mp4 (10m), compat-matrix-v1.csv (prompt-level status). Proposed test matrix attached as proposed-test-matrix.xlsx.

Ask: Please confirm you want us to run (1) and (2) this week — if yes, share an API key / test token for a staging project and an S3 bucket or URL for the 5k prompt set. If you prefer, we can run an initial subset (500 prompts) and share the diff.

Next meeting suggestion: 30min async readout of results on Tuesday 2026-10-06 10:00 PT — we can convert to a working session if there are >10 flagged prompts.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

From: Sara Kaplan <sara@bluewave.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Li <alex.li@bluewave.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interop showcase readout + concrete next-tests for migration proof

Jordan —

Great summary, thanks. We’re aligned on the ask. A few quick notes:
- We want you to run (1) the 5k set but we can start you with a 500-prompt subset this week to unblock investigation.
- For (2) SDK swap smoke: Alex will own running the shim against our CI. Alex — can you take that on?
- Budget: this will be run in a staging account; no billing impact to prod.

Sara
Director, Product Engineering | BlueWave Media

Quick technical plan + minimal data request below (so we can run the 500 prompt subset asap). I attached a simple XLS with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_schema, seq_length_est, notes.

Steps I’ll run this week:
- Ingest 500 prompts into our test harness (will use staging API key you give us).
- Run OpenAI-compat endpoint and log: full token stream, final JSON payload, and timing points (send->first-token, first->last-token).
- Diff pass: token-level compare + JSON-schema compare with your expected output. Flagged prompts will be triaged with you.

Data we need from BlueWave (minimal):
- Staging API key (scoped to a non-prod project) or a signed URL to upload the prompt CSV.
- A sample of the client code path you use for streaming (if you can share the SDK snippet that wires onmessage / ondata). If you cannot share code, a short description of backoff/retry policy will help.

Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
